title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this manuscript Grothendieck is setting up an intrinsic formalism for the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. the boundary of a compactification with normal-crossings-type strata. He describes the boundary by a system of spaces indexed by multiplicity:
- D_0 = X, the ambient space.
- D_d, the 'normalised' locus of d-fold points.
- D_{d,d'}, for d ≥ d', the space of pairs (a d-fold point, a choice of d' of its branches), with maps D_{d,d'} → D_d and D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}.
- D_d^!, a principal S_d-bundle over D_d whose fibre is the set of orderings of the d branches.
The identifications D_{d,0} ≅ D_d and the maps D_d → D_0 = X make D an object over X (178–179).

This page.
1. Base change of local properties. From the cartesian square of the previous page he concludes: if D_d → D_0 and D_{d'} → D_0 are local immersions (resp. local étale coverings), so is D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}.
2. Codimension. In the smooth case, codim(D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}) = codim(D_d → D_0) − codim(D_{d'} → D_0). He then imposes axiom (180): D_d → D_0 has codimension d.
3. A sharper, pointwise version of (180). For x ∈ D_d, let I_x be the set of liftings of x to D_{d,1} over D_1, i.e. the fibre (D_{d,1})_x, the set of branches through x. It should have cardinality d, and (181) the fibre (D_d^!)_x should be the set of bijections {1..d} → I_x. So D_d^! is the torsor of orderings of the local branches.
4. Local branches. Locally there are sections s_i : D_d → D_{d,1}, one for each i ∈ I_x. The composites D_d → D_{d,1} → D_1 → X all equal the canonical map i_d. The germs x_i = s_i(x) in D_1 give germs of subspaces D_x^i of X at the image point a; this is continued on the next page.
5. The axiom to be imposed (next page). The germ of D_d at x should be the transversal intersection of the d branch germs D_x^i.

In modern terms this is a non-embedded, intrinsic definition of a 'normal crossings configuration given by its normalised strata'. It covers immersed curves with nodes, which are not divisors on X with normal crossings. The next page attaches to D_d:
- the local system T_d = D_d^! ∧^{S_d} Z^d;
- the torus G_d = T_d ⊗ G_m.
These model the local monodromy / normal torus at the d-fold boundary strata, as needed for the 'structure at infinity' (tubular neighbourhoods, Dehn twists).
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The codimension-difference statement implicitly needs d ≥ d' and smoothness (stated).
Notation (181) is garbled: the intended meaning is that (D_d^!)_x is the set of bijections from {1..d} to I_x (an S_d-torsor), not a power Γ^{(I_x)}.
The previous page repeats 'D_{d',0} → D_0' twice where one should read D_{d,0} → D_0. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Intrinsic description of a normal-crossings boundary by the tower of normalised multiplicity strata D_d, the branch-choice spaces D_{d,d'}, and S_d-torsors D_d^! of branch orderings, with axioms of local immersion, codimension d, and transversality of branches
ideas.modern_name: Normalised strata of a normal crossings divisor (Deligne's D̃^{(p)} with orientation local systems ε^p); semi-simplicial/Δ-complex resolution of an snc/nc divisor; 'virtual' or immersed normal crossings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971) for the normalised strata and orientation sheaves; later log-geometry formalisms (Kato, Illusie) and boundary-stratum formalisms for M̄_{g,n} (Knudsen, Deligne–Mumford, graph-indexed strata)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. XIII (Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental group near a normal crossings divisor) treats related settings, but not this axiomatic tower as far as I know

ideas.what: Base change of local immersions / local coverings through the cartesian square, and additivity of codimension codim(D_{d,d'}→D_{d'}) = d − d'
ideas.modern_name: Stability of étale/unramified morphisms under base change; codimension of strata

ideas.what: Fibre of the S_d-torsor at x identified with orderings of the set I_x of branches through x, I_x ≅ (D_{d,1})_x
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of orderings of local branches (orientation/monodromy data of normal crossings)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an axiomatics of normal crossings that does not require an embedded divisor. Data and axioms are given on the normalised strata D_d themselves (local immersions, codimension d, transversal intersection of branch germs, S_d-torsors of orderings). It was intended as the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}. This anticipates the intrinsic 'stratified/log' descriptions of the Deligne–Mumford boundary, but the idea itself is essentially covered by Deligne's Hodge II and later log geometry.
missed.quote: (180) D_d → D_0 est de codim d ... I_x = ensemble des relèvements de x dans D_{d,1} au-dessus de D_1 ≃ (D_{d,1})_x
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it shows Grothendieck's route to the boundary of M_{g,ν} through an intrinsic, immersion-tolerant normal-crossings formalism. Mathematically it is subsumed by existing theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a clean axiomatics of normal-crossings strata (codimension, torsors of branch orderings, transversality). It is careful but essentially standard and paralleled by Deligne's Hodge II and later log/stratification formalisms. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: First line probably: '(i.e. on a un rev. étale dans un vois. loc.)'.
(181) should be read as (D_d^!)_x ≃ Isom({1,…,d}, I_x), the bijections onto I_x, rather than 'Γ^{(I_x)}'.
'(dimension croissante ! (?))' is plausibly 'codimension croissante' or similar, in the context of axiom (180).
In (182) the reading is 'I_x = ensemble des relèvements de x dans D_{d,1} au-dessus de D_1 ≃ (D_{d,1})_x'.
'les germes x_i de x dans D_1 pr. les s_i' means 'germs x_i image of x in D_1 under the s_i'.
